story.head: Open season on the Flames’ net
paras: The Kings are on a three-game losing streak, and the Flames (8-10-1) lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Wednesday. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames sixth (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (30th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.

The Flames’ record (.447) is about what their chances are worth. The Kings have played better than their record (.353) says: their chances are worth about .629, and their finishing has held them back.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd), take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and take more penalties than they draw (31st). On the other side, the Kings leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). They also keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd), so good looks are likely to be hard to come by for the Flames. The Kings are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring.

Dustin Wolf (3-5-1 / .869 SV% in 9 GS) has struggled for Calgary so far, but will likely start. Los Angeles has two options in net: Darcy Kuemper (5-5-1 / .873 SV% in 11 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-5-1 / .907 SV% in 6 GS). Kuemper has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Wolf has a .958 save percentage in five starts against the Kings, well above his usual .898. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
